title: csm Skill Suite Completion-Defect Analysis (extends the csm-plan/csm-build finding)

tldr.content: Extension of the 2026-09-14 csm-plan/csm-build finding to the whole csm suite. The same defect classes recur, skill-specifically: (1) the identical step-4 'end the invocation' bootstrap is in SEVEN more skills (8 total); (2) every non-orchestrate skill self-judges its terminal decision; (3) the canonical JSON records (plan/review/approach/research/build-state/builds/tests/norms/doctrine/upload/browse) are ungated — check-suite validates only legacy Markdown and csm-skill-progress; (4) csm-orchestrate stops the whole run on the first node failure with no continuation or supersession; (5) legal SAVED/INCOMPLETE terminators and iteration caps; (6) corpus shows predecessor records orphaned after successors complete. All 14 prior claims are carried verbatim; mitigations already exist in csm-bdd-tdd (typed supersession), csm-autoresearch (separate evaluator), csm-orchestrate (independent final review) and should be generalized.

executiveSummary.content:
This finding EXTENDS the prior csm-plan/csm-build analysis to all 14 csm skills without dropping any prior claim (all are carried verbatim in `claims` and `references`). Four tracks: per-skill SKILL.md comparison (R1), executable enforcement map (R2), coordinator + self (R3), corpus evidence (R4).

```text
Prior finding (csm-plan/build) -> R1 all SKILL.md -> R2 enforcement map
  -> R3 csm-orchestrate + csm-deep-research -> R4 corpus
  -> Synthesis (prior claims imported) -> Challenge -> Judge -> Verified finding
```

Headline: the defect classes are suite-wide, not csm-plan/csm-build-specific. The strongest new result is enforcement: check-suite gates only legacy Markdown and progress; the canonical JSON records are unvalidated, and csm-orchestrate does not enforce completion of the skills it routes to.

keyFindings.content:
K1. supported — the tmux step-4 'end the invocation' bootstrap is in 7 more skills (8 total) [ref-csm-review][ref-csm-deep-research].
K2. supported — terminal completion is primary-owned except csm-orchestrate (independent final review) and csm-autoresearch (separate evaluator); deep-research/review add independent intermediate evaluation [ref-adversarial-review][ref-csm-autoresearch].
K3. supported — canonical JSON records are ungated; only legacy Markdown + progress are validated [ref-check-suite].
K4. supported — csm-orchestrate terminates the run on the first node failure with no continuation/supersession [ref-csm-orchestrate][ref-co-recovery].
K5. supported — csm-grill terminates only on user agreement (prose, no gate) [ref-csm-grill].
K6. supported — corpus: predecessor progress/build-state/plan records are orphaned after successors complete [ref-prior-finding].
K7. supported — 5 record classes are unmapped/ungated; guard tests are orphaned [ref-agents-index][ref-check-suite].
K8. supported — mitigations already exist (bdd-tdd typed supersession; autoresearch separate evaluator; orchestrate independent review) and should be generalized [ref-csm-bdd-tdd][ref-csm-orchestrate].
K9. (prior, carried) acceptance-signal validation gap + status-only Completion Gate let completed tasks carry unbuilt deliverables [ref-prior-finding].
K10. (prior, carried) the build-state cursor pins nextTransition to the first transition; the durable record is left unclosed [ref-prior-finding].

detailSections.content:
D1 Per-skill applicability matrix (P1 weak exit criteria; P2 record ungated; P3/'do-not-stop' prose; P4 tmux end-invocation; P5 missing supersession; P6 stop forks; P7 self-judged):
- csm-grill: P1 M, P2 M, P3 H, P5 M, P7 H.
- csm-review: P1 M, P2 L, P4 H, P5 M, P6 H, P7 H.
- csm-review-python: P1 M, P4 H, P5 M, P6 M, P7 H.
- csm-scan: P1 M, P4 H, P5 M, P6 M, P7 H.
- csm-ddd: P1 M, P5 M, P6 M, P7 H.
- csm-bdd-tdd: P4 H, P6 M, P7 H (P5 mitigated: typed supersession pointer).
- csm-make-tests: P1 M, P4 H, P5 M, P6 H, P7 H.
- csm-autoresearch: P6 M only (P7 mitigated: separate evaluator).
- csm-orchestrate: P6 M, P7 L (independent final review); no tmux.
- csm-deep-research: P1 M, P2 H, P4 H, P5 M, P6 H, P7 M.
[R1, all SKILL.md refs]

D2 Enforcement map: check-suite (make check) is the only corpus gate; it validates plans/reviews/approaches/research as `*-*.md`, plus progress JSON. The JSON canonical equivalents and build-state/builds are unscanned; `.agents/tests|norms|doctrine|upload|browse` are unmapped so they fail index mapping if tracked [ref-check-suite][ref-agents-index].

D3 Coordinator: per-node cursor lifecycle; a single node failure sets phaseFailure and returns a terminal receipt, abandoning pending nodes and later phases; maxAttempts default 2; resume reconciles but never retries a terminal child [ref-csm-orchestrate][ref-co-recovery].

D4 Corpus: 29 progress records (csm-build 17, csm-plan 6, csm-deep-research 5, csm-review 1) — only 4/14 skills emit a progress tracker; 23 build-state (COMPLETE 5, BLOCKED 9, CHECKPOINT 5, RECOVER 3, SELECT 1 → 9/23 non-terminal, 18/23 non-COMPLETE); 60 JSON plans (30 complete/17 in_progress/9 ready/4 blocked); 3/4 machine reviews INCOMPLETE [R4].

D5 Mitigations to generalize: csm-bdd-tdd typed supersession pointer; csm-autoresearch separate evaluator; csm-orchestrate mandatory independent final review with provenance gating [ref-csm-bdd-tdd][ref-csm-autoresearch][ref-csm-orchestrate][ref-adversarial-review].

D6 No completion check: corpus validation checks presence, not evidence, of task completion [ref-check-suite].

PRIOR FINDING (carried verbatim, not restated): all prior detail sections, claims claim-tmux..claim-efficacy-unverified, remain authoritative in the prior document and are imported here.

recommendation.content:
Recommend: generalize the prior fixes suite-wide and add the missing cross-skill enforcement. Confidence: high on the enforcement gaps; medium on efficacy until trialed. All prior recommendation items remain valid (imported).

Cross-skill fixes (in priority order):
1. Make check-suite validate the CANONICAL JSON records (plans/reviews/approaches/research) and csm-build-state/builds/tests/norms/doctrine/upload/browse, not just legacy Markdown; add the missing index sections [K3][K7].
2. Make tmux bootstrap conditional in all 8 skills, and never end an invocation with a non-terminal control/record unless a PAUSED/BLOCKED checkpoint is written [K1].
3. Separate the stop decision from the worker in every long-running skill (a deterministic Stop-gate + independent evaluator), generalizing csm-orchestrate's independent final review and csm-autoresearch's separate evaluator [K2][K8].
4. Make csm-orchestrate continue (or explicitly surface a resumable supersession) on a node failure instead of terminating the run with pending nodes/phases [K4].
5. Add a terminal `superseded`/`abandoned` state and require a closure flip when a run is displaced by a successor; generalize csm-bdd-tdd's enforced typed supersession pointer (and csm-review's unused field) to plans/progress/build-state [K6][K8].
6. Give csm-grill a deterministic confirmation gate (or an evaluator) rather than relying on user sentiment [K5].
7. Wire the orphaned guard tests (csm-review / csm-review-python producer-validation) into CI [K7].
8. Verify task/step completion against evidence, not presence [D6].

What would change the answer: a controlled trial showing the fixes do not reduce stops per run. Cost of being wrong: suite-wide churn where records are orphaned and features are closed as complete while unbuilt.

unverifiedClaims.content: U1. Whether the suite-wide fixes empirically reduce premature stops needs a controlled trial. U2. For skills with no machine artifact (grill/make-tests/autoresearch/bdd/ddd/scan/upload), unfinished work cannot be proven from artifacts; the missing-artifact gap is the finding, not a count. U3. Review INCOMPLETE denotes coverage caveats, not necessarily abandoned remediation. U4. Prior finding's unresolved items (see prior doc) remain unresolved here.

processAppendix.content: DEEP x hybrid; extends the 2026-09-14 finding (run-20260914t060000z-csmplanbuildmeta, digest sha256:ac7c4b7541ad712c5ba36fe0f866091d523bd289be755e0bf8f374779ae8610a) with ALL prior claims imported verbatim (nothing dropped). Tracks R1-R4 (per-skill SKILL.md, enforcement map, coordinator/self, corpus). Independent challenger and judge; VERIFY primary-personal.

claims.statement: csm-build's Tmux Session Bootstrap is the mandated first step and step 4 says to end the invocation when a detached session was launched; on a host without an already-active tmux session the normal case hits this and the current invocation ends before execution — although the intent is that the detached session runs the build.

citations.quote: If a new detached session was launched, end the invocation — tmux does the build from the start.

claims.statement: The canonical build-state cursor is inconsistent with the SKILL: the validator pins control.nextTransition to the FIRST transition of the current state, so a record parked at CHECKPOINT must declare 'CHECKPOINT -> SELECT' even though the SKILL tells the agent to choose SELECT/COMPLETE/BLOCKED and record the exact next transition. CHECKPOINT->COMPLETE itself is legal and tested (state.mjs:38; build-json-control.test.mjs), so the defect is a cursor-vocabulary mismatch, not a rejected transition.

citations.quote: next transition does not match the lifecycle state
walks CHECKPOINT -> COMPLETE and asserts validity
From CHECKPOINT, transition to SELECT, COMPLETE, or BLOCKED

claims.statement: The 'do not stop after one task or cycle' rule is prose-only: no gate enforces continuation or task completion, and the plan-corpus gate in check-suite only covers '*-csm.md' projections, so the canonical 'csm-plan/1' JSON corpus (60 files) is not validated by CI.

citations.quote: Do not stop after one task or cycle

claims.statement: csm-build's executable input gate requires all five inputs (plan/bdd/tests/ddd/norms) unconditionally, while the SKILL labels only DDD/norms optional (NORMS.md 'entirely optional') and treats plan/bdd/tests as required; and the current-context executor auto-walks INTEGRATE->CHECKPOINT->COMPLETE via completeBuild without evaluating Completion Gate conditions 1-8.

The strongest single cause is a validation/enforcement gap: csm-plan's SKILL mandates exactly one positive runnable acceptance signal (SKILL.md:358), but the schema only requires a non-empty string (csm-plan.schema.json:109) and no lint rejects disjunctive 'Either ... OR record/document/keep a deferral' signals; csm-build Completion Gate #1 then reads task STATUS, so tasks are marked completed with the feature unbuilt (observed in 5 tasks across the two 2026-09-14 DWRR plans).

citations.quote: the one runnable command/test whose pass objectively proves this task done
Either ... OR the opt-in decision is explicitly recorded
OR the scope decision ... is explicitly recorded
Every numbered task is completed or explicitly excluded

claims.statement: Successor-plan proliferation is enabled by the absence of a typed in-artifact supersession field: csm-plan.schema.json is additionalProperties:false with no supersedes/supersededBy property, while csm-build looks for a 'typed supersession pointer' in the descriptor. Supersession is nonetheless resolvable out-of-band via .agents/README.md prose and 'closed as superseded' nextTransition strings; the dynamic-worker-runtime goal spans 21 plans (12 frozen siblings).

citations.quote: Check the selected JSON descriptor for its typed supersession pointer

claims.statement: The corpus shows records left unclosed: 9 plans marked complete still carry open tasks; 3 non-complete plans carry no status:'pending' tasks (though they hold in_progress/blocked tasks, so they are not simply 'done-but-unclosed'); and build-state records are 9/23 non-terminal (BLOCKED is terminal, so 14/23 terminal). Aggregate: 60 plans, 429 tasks, 198 pending, 230 open.

Commit policy is a static string ('commits: disabled') with no commit-ledger field in the plan schema; 34/60 plans are 'disabled' (9/14 recent completes) even though the work was committed by successors, so the record cannot distinguish uncommitted work and stalls at CHECKPOINT.

csm-plan's planning terminal (SAVED) is not the artifact's terminal: plans are born ready/NOT_STARTED and only a later human message starts them, with no owner/trigger; 9 plans are ready/NOT_STARTED carrying 57 status:'pending' tasks.

Applicability obligations form a mostly unclosed second gate: across 54 applicability records (52 warranted), 51 keep every obligation 'required' and only 1 carries 'satisfied' obligations; neither skill instructs an obligation-status update at CHECKPOINT, and Completion Gate #1 does not consult obligations.

Legal low-evidence stop forks exist: 'incomplete' is an accepted executor status with no repair path; REPAIR stops after two attempts; broad BLOCKED rules; and the orchestrate handoff retries at most maxAttempts (default 2, csm-orchestrate/lib/recovery.mjs).

citations.quote: After two failed attempts ... stop patching

claims.statement: External practice separates the stop decision from the worker: a deterministic Stop hook runs a check as a script and blocks the turn from ending until it passes (8-block override), and TaskCompleted can prevent a task being marked complete; /goal uses a separate evaluator model that sends the agent back to work. csm-build has none of these — the stop decision is self-judged at CHECKPOINT and enforcement is prose-only; it also has no run-level no-progress/budget ceiling.

citations.quote: a Stop hook runs your check as a script and blocks the turn from ending until it passes
a small fast model checks whether the condition holds ... starts another turn

claims.statement: The canonical csm-plan/1 JSON plans are ungated: check-suite's plan-corpus loop filters files ending '-csm.md', so the authoritative JSON plans (60 files) escape Control/journal/task validation in CI — drift in the durable record is invisible.

Whether fixing these instruction-level issues actually makes a csm-build run continue to completion is not yet demonstrated; it requires a controlled trial (apply the fixes, run a plan to COMPLETE, measure stops per run).

The identical step-4 sentence "end the invocation — tmux does the X from the start" appears in SEVEN more skills besides csm-build — csm-plan, csm-review, csm-review-python, csm-scan, csm-bdd-tdd, csm-make-tests, and csm-deep-research (8 SKILL.md files total) — so any of them can end before work runs when no tmux session is active; only the step-4 sentence is template-identical (step 3 varies).

citations.quote: end the invocation — tmux does the review from the start
end the invocation — tmux does the analysis from the start
end the invocation — tmux does the scan from the start
end the invocation — tmux does the mutation from the start
end the invocation — tmux does the generation from the start
end the invocation — tmux does the research from the start

claims.statement: The terminal completion decision is primary-owned in every skill except csm-orchestrate and csm-autoresearch, which mitigate it structurally (mandatory independent final review / separate evaluator owning candidate status). Independent INTERMEDIATE evaluation also exists in csm-deep-research (independent challenger + judge) and csm-review (independent challengers) but does not own the terminal decision.

check-suite's corpus gate validates only legacy Markdown (*-csm.md, *-review.md, *-approach.md, *-research.md); the canonical JSON records — plan/review/approach/research and csm-build-state/builds — are never parsed, so the authoritative artifacts are ungated and drift is invisible to CI. The only JSON record class content-gated is csm-skill-progress/1.

Five record classes have no .agents index section and no content gate — .agents/tests, .agents/norms, .agents/doctrine, .agents/upload, .agents/browse — so csm-make-tests / csm-scan / csm-review-python / csm-upload / csm-browse records are unvalidated (and some are blocked from landing by the unmapped-section hard fail).

citations.quote: agentsIndexSectionFor returns null for these classes

claims.statement: Guard tests that would validate csm-review and csm-review-python records exist and pass but are referenced by no Makefile/CI target and are invisible to the orphan check (which scans only tests/**), so the records remain effectively unguarded.

The single coordination entry point csm-orchestrate stops the phase and whole run on the FIRST node failure, leaving later nodes and phases unrun; it performs only a bounded retry (maxAttempts default 2) with no continuation past an exhausted node and no typed supersession of the abandoned work — so it does not enforce completion of the skills it routes to.

Multiple skills reach a legal terminal without full delivery: csm-review proceeds to SAVED after three distinct VERIFY failures; csm-deep-research proceeds to SAVED after its VERIFY budget; csm-make-tests terminates generation at a fixed iteration cap and records skips; INCOMPLETE/BLOCKED are legal terminals for review/review-python/scan/make-tests.

citations.quote: after three distinct failures ... proceeds to SAVED

claims.statement: csm-grill's loop terminates only on user sentiment — 'keep cycling until the user explicitly agrees' — pure prose with no deterministic gate and no independent evaluator; its artifact is schema-referenced but ungated.

citations.quote: keep cycling until the user explicitly agrees; loop until explicit agreement; Exit: user explicitly agrees

claims.statement: Corpus evidence: predecessor progress records are orphaned rather than closed — active trackers (broker-upstream 39%, dwrr-final-residuals 92%, dynamic-worker-runtime-build 73%, dwrr-drift-build 80%) stay active after successor runs complete; commit 284f277 declares a plan COMPLETE while the orchestrate-request-intake-router tracker is still 92% active. Five 2026-09-12 DWRR build-state records remain in_progress (18/23 build-state records are non-COMPLETE; 9/23 are non-terminal, since BLOCKED is terminal).
3 of 4 machine review reports are INCOMPLETE and the review schema has no remediation-closure field, so closure can only be confirmed indirectly via commits; two audits have no visible close-out.

Only 4 of 14 skills emit an .agents/progress tracker (csm-build 17, csm-plan 6, csm-deep-research 5, csm-review 1); every skill produces some durable JSON artifact, so per-run abandonment is not machine-visible for the other 10 skills — the missing progress record is the gap, not the absence of any artifact.

Three structural mitigations already exist and should be generalized: csm-bdd-tdd carries the only ENFORCED typed supersession pointer (the plan-descriptor pointer csm-build follows); csm-autoresearch gives status to a separate evaluator; csm-orchestrate mandates an independent final review (provenance host-backed/in-process-independent). csm-review additionally DECLARES a typed supersedesArtifactId that is unused.

No corpus path verifies task/step completion against evidence: plan validation checks only the presence of a Task ID and a non-empty Acceptance signal, and journal rows only that Next state is in the machine enum.

citations.quote: only Task ID + Acceptance signal presence

claims.statement: csm-review's canonical findings schema declares an optional typed supersedesArtifactId field (csm-review/schemas/csm-review-findings.schema.json:245) that is neither exercised by tests nor referenced by SKILL.md — an unused supersession field, so typed supersession is not universally absent across the suite.
